rules.name: Resolve genuinely ambiguous references
rules.guidance: Clarify a pronoun or demonstrative only when its intended referent is unambiguous from the surrounding context.
apply_when: A reference has multiple plausible interpretations.
do_not_apply_when: Naming a referent would require an assumption.
preservation: Keep the original claim and scope.

rules.name: Make a phrase clearer without rebuilding the sentence
rules.guidance: Replace or trim a local phrase when it is wordy, vague, grammatically awkward, or unnecessarily indirect. Preserve the surrounding sentence structure whenever possible.
apply_when: A phrase-level issue can be fixed locally.
do_not_apply_when: The phrase is already clear and appropriate.
A local edit would distort the intended relationship.
preservation: Keep the original proposition, emphasis, and qualifications.

rules.name: Prefer precise wording over vague wording
rules.guidance: Replace imprecise wording only when the source provides enough information to make the wording more exact.
apply_when: A phrase is unnecessarily broad or unclear.
do_not_apply_when: A more specific phrase would add information not present in the source.
preservation: Do not strengthen, weaken, or expand claims.

rules.name: Make supported logical relationships clear
rules.guidance: Clarify cause, contrast, sequence, or qualification only when that relationship is supported by the surrounding text.
apply_when: The relationship between adjacent ideas is difficult to follow.
do_not_apply_when: The relationship is uncertain or would need an assumption.
preservation: Do not invent causal links or conclusions.

rules.name: Remove true redundancy
rules.guidance: Remove repeated information that adds no emphasis, qualification, or technical meaning.
apply_when: The same point is repeated without a clear purpose.
do_not_apply_when: Repetition is required for precision, safety, legal meaning, or readability.
preservation: Retain every distinct condition and qualification.

rules.name: Respect document genre and audience
rules.guidance: Match formality, detail, structure, and terminology to the document type and intended reader.
apply_when: The document genre and audience are known.
do_not_apply_when: The genre or audience is unknown; use a conservative edit.
preservation: Do not make academic or technical text casual without instruction.

rules.name: Preserve evidence and uncertainty
rules.guidance: Retain citations, numerical results, limitations, uncertainty, and the strength of the original claim.
apply_when: Editing sentences that contain evidence, results, or qualifications.
do_not_apply_when: A citation or result appears incomplete; flag it rather than repairing it by guesswork.
preservation: Never fabricate citations, measurements, findings, or certainty.

rules.name: Improve paragraph focus only when needed
rules.guidance: Keep each paragraph centred on a coherent idea and preserve the progression of the source argument.
apply_when: A paragraph combines unrelated ideas or lacks a clear progression.
do_not_apply_when: The original structure is required by a template, standard, or list format.
preservation: Do not move claims in a way that changes their evidential context.
